title: Give a toddler manikin a 5 mL dose with an oral syringe: tip between the gums and cheek, given in small squirts
instruction: Give the toddler care manikin its 5 mL practice dose (water) with the oral syringe, then put the syringe back on its rests in the tray.
context: Giving a small child liquid medicine with an oral syringe is something most parents have done. Great Ormond Street Hospital's leaflet: "Put the tip of the oral syringe inside your child's mouth between the gums and the inside surface of their cheek"; "Gently push the plunger to squirt small amounts"; "Allow your child to swallow before you carry on"; "Do not squirt the entire dose into your child's mouth in one go" (they may choke). ASHP: "Never squirt the liquid ... directly onto the back of a child's throat." The tip has to go in at the corner of the open mouth and sit in the 4 to 7 mm pocket between the side teeth and the cheek, pressing the cheek a little, with the barrel slanted toward the cheek, not down the middle toward the throat. A gripper holding the barrel cannot also push the plunger (a person uses the thumb), so one hand keeps the tip in place, taking the plunger's friction, while the other pushes it in 1 mL steps with pauses.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, z up from the table top. (1) Toddler care manikin head (2 to 3 years: head 16.8 cm long, 13.4 cm wide, face 8.2 cm nasal root to chin), upright on a 3 cm stand (fixed), face toward the robot; nasal root at x 31.0, y 0, z 20.0; mouth open 4.6 x 2.6 cm, its middle 15 cm up. Inside: 20 primary teeth on upper and lower gum ridges (outer faces of the side teeth 14 to 19.5 mm from the midline), tongue, throat, and soft inner cheeks (faces 21.5 mm from the midline, giving outward 0.06 N/mm). (2) 5 mL oral syringe (like BD 305218), filled to 5 mL (water): barrel 14 mm across, 58 mm long, 4.5 mm tip 10 mm long, flange 30 mm; plunger out 52 mm, 0.8 N friction; 21 g. It lies on two notched rests (2.2 cm high, under the barrel's front and the flange) on an 11 x 4.4 cm tray at x 20.0, y 12.0 (fixed), tip forward at x 25.5. Arms at the ready pose, grippers open. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot. Real build: print the head (two halves, teeth arches, sprung cheek plates), its stand with the two drain wells and the tray from the STL files in print/ (made from the simulated geometry by make_print_parts.py; parts, springs and numbered assembly steps in README, "Building it for real").
scoring: Every step, plunger travel (0.113 mL/mm) is booked where the tip is: cheek pocket (2 to 24 mm behind the nasal root, at least 0.5 mm outside the side teeth's outer faces, pressing the cheek out 0.5 mm, 0.11 N), toward the throat (inside the row of teeth or behind the last molar) or spilled. A squirt is travel between pauses (1 s with under 0.5 mm of travel). Partial credit is only the dose in the pocket: 0.8 x (pocket mL / 4.7), at most 0.8; spilled or throat water earns nothing. 1.0 (held 1 s) needs at least 4.7 mL in the pocket, no fault, and the syringe back on its rests: released (no gripper within 4 cm), tip forward (within 10 deg), tip within 8 mm of its start, the barrel's axis 30.8 to 36.8 mm up at tip and flange (33.8 mm in the notches), still 1 s. A fault (a squirt over 1.5 mL, over 0.2 mL toward the throat, over 0.3 mL spilled) caps the score at 0.5; over 1.5 mL toward the throat (choking) scores 0. Real trial: water; the printed head drains both cheek pockets to well A and the throat to well B of its stand by separate bores; weigh each well and the syringe before and after (spilled = given - A - B); squirts and pauses from a side video against the 0.2 mL marks; a photo shows the syringe in both notches.
reset_notes: Lift the head off its stand, empty wells A and B, run 2 mL of water through each cheek pocket and the throat, wait 2 minutes and empty the wells again; wipe the mouth and chin dry and replace the bib; set the head back on its pins; refill the syringe with water to the 5 mL line (no air), weigh it, lay it on its rests tip forward. Simulation: each trial starts the simulator afresh.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 20 Hz control. Head skin and lining are one fixed mesh; teeth, gums and tongue are boxes; each inner cheek is a plate on a sprung slide (0.06 N/mm, estimate). No liquid: the dose is the plunger's travel (12.0 mm bore), booked by where the tip is; the plunger slides with 0.8 N friction (estimate). The child does not move or swallow. The printed head books water by where it drains, not by the tip's press.
